summary: The note previews a season of classical music and opera festivals, each combining performance with education. It covers the Bel Canto Classical Music Festival, Midnight Opera Festival, Sacred Echoes Music Festival, String Quartet Autumn Serenade and Fresh Sound Festival, running from September to late November. It argues these festivals preserve musical heritage and build community and appreciation.
one_line: A preview of autumn classical music and opera festivals, from Bel Canto to Fresh Sound, highlighting their performances, educational programs, and cultural role.
key_facts: The Bel Canto Classical Music Festival starts September 15 at the Valerius Opera House and lasts ten days.
Violinist Emily Tan, praised for her rendition of Bach's Partitas, is a featured performer at the Bel Canto festival.
Maestro Antonio DiLorenzo, composer and conductor, presents a masterclass on Vivaldi's compositions at the Bel Canto festival.
The Midnight Opera Festival opens September 28 at the Elysian Park Amphitheater, an outdoor venue.
Soprano Giovanna Ricci leads a performance of Puccini's 'La Bohème' at the Midnight Opera Festival.
The Sacred Echoes Music Festival begins October 12, runs five days at St. Cecilia Cathedral, and focuses on spiritually inspired works.
Professor Helena Brigsley lectures on the history of sacred music, from Gregorian chants to contemporary compositions.
The 'Voices of Angels' choir, directed by Thomas Keller, performs Mozart's 'Requiem' as the Sacred Echoes highlight.
The String Quartet Autumn Serenade starts November 3 at the Mélange Art Center, known for bold architecture and state-of-the-art acoustics.
Luthier and music historian Sarah Ming leads a seminar on the evolution of string instruments.
The Adler String Quartet premieres a newly commissioned work by composer Jonathan Hughes.
The Fresh Sound Festival kicks off November 29 and showcases contemporary composers rooted in classical techniques.
Composer Elise Alexander's avant-garde symphony 'Time's Tapestry' blends electronic music with live orchestration.
The Fresh Sound Festival offers workshops, open rehearsals, and interactive discussions to dispel myths about the inaccessibility of classical music.
